Campaign brief: For engineers constrained by a hosted platform’s built-in email sender, Resend provides a separate platform for personalized, event-driven transactional email; paid Resend plans have no daily email limit.
events.reader:
Selected audience: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does.
Situation context (grounded; check applicability): Individual engineers integrating a hosted auth platform (Supabase Auth) into a product's signup, password-reset, invite, and OTP flows post first-person accounts, in GitHub issues and discussions on the platform's own repos, of hitting the built-in email rate limit and having to reason through Supabase's dashboard logs, SMTP settings, and plan tiers themselves to diagnose it.
events.reader_segment: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does
events.promise: For engineers constrained by a hosted platform’s built-in email sender, Resend provides a separate platform for personalized, event-driven transactional email; paid Resend plans have no daily email limit.
events.arc: Move the problem-aware reader from recognizing the limit of the built-in sender, to understanding what Resend is and why its launch is relevant, to a bounded first setup step that does not overstate compatibility or production readiness.

emails.job: Announce Resend and earn a free signup from a non-customer who wants to evaluate a separate transactional sender for auth-related email.
emails.single_idea: Resend is now available as a separate platform for event-driven transactional email; for engineers running into built-in sender limits, the material difference is that paid Resend plans have no daily email limit.
emails.objection: A separate sender is only useful if it does not simply exchange one hard cap for another or leave the hosted platform’s own limit unresolved.
must_not_say: Do not claim Resend automatically raises or bypasses the hosted auth platform’s own dashboard rate limit; that setting still has to be changed manually.
Do not claim the Free plan removes daily sending limits; it is capped at 100 emails per day.
Do not claim Resend detects, prevents, or survives an upstream Auth Hook wiping SMTP configuration.
Do not claim Resend explains or corrects how another platform meters email against its rate limit.
Do not promise a native Supabase integration, drop-in compatibility, unchanged application behavior, or a complete migration time.
Do not promise uninterrupted auth email, guaranteed inbox placement, or guaranteed deliverability.
Do not imply transactional and marketing sending are isolated by account or infrastructure; dedicated IP isolation is a separate Scale-level add-on.
Do not dilute the announcement with Broadcasts, Automations, Dedicated IPs, customer-logo lists, security claims, or the full SDK catalog.

Resend is a separate provider, not a change to the auth platform's own limiter: the platform's dashboard rate limit still has to be raised by hand after wiring SMTP, and Resend's own free tier reimposes a 100-emails-a-day cap.

Only the paid tiers remove the daily cap; on the free plan the engineer swaps one 100/day ceiling for another, and nothing in the ledger speaks to the auth platform's own rate-limit setting that still has to be raised.
emails.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
emails.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
emails.why_it_fails: Waiting and retrying do not change the built-in sender’s limit, and upgrading the hosted platform’s plan may not raise it; using a separate sender also requires the platform’s own rate-limit setting to be adjusted manually.
emails.mechanism: Resend handles personalized, event-driven transactional email through a verified domain and API key. Its Free plan is capped at 100 emails per day, while Pro, Scale, and Enterprise have no daily email limit.
emails.next_step_decision: Whether to begin a scoped Resend setup for transactional email rather than continuing to rely only on the hosted platform’s built-in sender.
emails.next_step_value: Create the account needed to begin setup with the team’s own verified domain and a Resend API key.
emails.next_step_limit: Signup does not prove compatibility with the hosted auth workflow, change its upstream rate-limit setting, or validate production delivery; the Free plan also remains capped at 100 emails per day.

alternative_arguments.single_idea: Resend can reduce the homegrown template machinery that accumulates around transactional email without requiring the engineer to give up code-based email content.
alternative_arguments.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
alternative_arguments.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
alternative_arguments.why_it_fails: As the number of messages grows, ad hoc template wiring and change tracking become an additional system the engineer has to maintain.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: React Email keeps content in code, while Resend Templates let the application send a template ID and variables; the editor adds autosaving, revision history, and a publish flow.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: adopting an email platform means fully outsourcing the team’s email program. After: the team can retain code-based content while moving template delivery and revision management into a defined workflow.
must_not_say: Do not claim Resend eliminates all in-house email work or fully replaces the team’s transactional-email system.
Do not promise unchanged application behavior, a drop-in migration, or a specific migration duration.
Do not claim that signup alone validates production delivery or the complete workflow.

The researched poster explicitly refuses to fully outsource the program, so only parts move: content stays in their own components, observability is bounded by 30-day data retention, and automation runs bill at $0.0015 each once the free.
alternative_arguments.objection: I do not want to fully outsource a transactional-email program that needs to remain close to the application code.
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Whether Resend’s React Email and Templates workflow is suitable for one existing transactional message before considering a broader migration.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: Review the documented model of keeping email content in React Email components while sending with a template ID and variables.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: Reviewing the documentation does not establish production behavior, complete migration effort, or compatibility with every part of the reader’s current system.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Frame the launch around taming transactional template sprawl while preserving code-based content; avoid a generic feature announcement or an absolute claim about eliminating maintenance.

events.subject: Send auth email with Resend
events.preview_text: Evaluate a separate sending platform with clear daily limits.
events.body:
Resend is now available as a separate platform for sending personalized, event-driven transactional email from your own verified domain.

If a hosted auth provider’s built-in sender constrains signup confirmations, password resets, invitations, or OTPs, you can evaluate Resend independently using a Resend API key.

The limits are explicit: the Free plan allows **100 emails per day**. Pro, Scale, and Enterprise plans have **no daily email limit**, so moving to a paid plan does not exchange one daily cap for another.

Resend does not change the auth platform’s own rate-limit setting. After configuring a separate sender, that setting still needs to be adjusted in the platform’s dashboard.

Create a free account to begin setup with your verified domain and API key.

events.message: Email 1, draft 1: "Beyond the Auth logs"
events.subject: Beyond the Auth logs
events.preview_text: Keep transactional email in code without maintaining every template revision yourself.
events.body:
Checking Auth logs can help explain a blocked signup, OTP, or magic-link email. It still leaves the template wiring and revision trail for each transactional message to maintain.

Resend is now available: an email sending platform for personalized, event-driven transactional email from your own verified domain using a Resend API key.

You can keep email content in React Email components, powered by Resend’s open source component library. When sending, your application passes a template ID and variables.

Resend Templates adds autosaving, full version history, and a publish flow in the editor. Content stays code-based while delivery and revisions move into a defined workflow.

Review the documentation to see whether this model fits one existing transactional message before considering a broader migration.
